{"id": "b0ffeb75-df07-4316-ba1a-d4b27c0f88e0", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_snmc6dSJiM23OtAXshruNX", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Route evaluation\",\"context\":\"# Route evaluation\\n\\nCloud WAN evaluates routes at each core network edge in the following order:\\n\\n1. The most specific route for the destination\\n2. For routes with the same destination IP address, but different targets, the\\n following route priority is used:\\n\\n 1. Static routes\\n 2. System routes. For more information, see Routing behavior for 1:1 NAT in AWS Cloud WAN.\\n 3. VPC-propagated routes in the same Region.\\n 4. For dynamic routes received at the core network with an\\n *unequal* AS path length and/or MED BGP\\n attributes, Cloud WAN evaluates them in the following order:\\n\\n 1. AS path length\\n 2. MED\\n 5. For dynamic routes received at the core network with\\n *equal* AS path length and MED BGP attributes,\\n Cloud WAN evaluates them in the following order:\\n\\n 1. Direct Connect gateway-propagated routes.\\n 2. Cloud WAN Connect-propagated routes in the same\\n Region.\\n 3. Site-to-Site VPN-propagated routes in the same\\n Region.\\n 4. Routes propagated from other sources, such as transit gateway peering\\n and core network edges in other remote Regions\\n over the AWS global infrastructure. If identical routes are\\n received from two or more sources, a single attachment will be\\n chosen in a deterministically random manner (this occurs on a per\\n segment/network function group basis so you could see different destinations\\n for the same route across different segment/network function groups)\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-route-evaluation.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Direct Connect gateway attachments in AWS Cloud WAN\",\"context\":\"## Route propagation\\n\\nA Direct Connect gateway attachments support BGP-based dynamic routing for both inbound and\\noutbound directions.\\n\\nFor inbound routes,\\n\\n* Cloud WAN learns BGP routes advertised from your on-premises location\\n via the Direct Connect gateway and the transit virtual interface. Routes are learnt\\n in the segment route-tables of the associated core network edges for the\\n attachment.\\n* Routes learned in segment route table can be routed across all\\n AWS Regions for that segment.\\n* Cloud WAN follows the route evaluation order for the same prefixes learned\\n over multiple attachments. See Route evaluation for\\n more information.\\n* Direct Connect gateway will advertise routes from all on-premises locations towards\\n all segment route-tables of the associated core network edges for the attachment.\\n\\nFor outbound routes,\\n\\n* Cloud WAN propagates routes from the segment route table to the Direct Connect\\n gateway, which in turn advertises these routes over transit virtual interfaces\\n to your on-premises locations via BGP.\\n* Each core network edge associated with the Direct Connect gateway attachment\\n advertises only its local routes towards the Direct Connect gateway.\\n* The AS_PATH BGP attribute is retained in these route advertisements to your\\n on-premises locations. For more information about AS_PATH and BGP, see Private virtual interface and transit virtual interface routing\\n policies in the *AWS Direct Connect User\\n Guide*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-dxattach-about.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"AWS Cloud WAN Routing policies\",\"context\":\"## Key considerations\\n\\nThe following is a list of considerations that should be taken into account before using Cloud WAN Routing Policies:\\n\\n### Route evaluation and ordering\\n\\n* Route summarization will remove all matched prefixes and replace them with a single summarized route. The summarized prefix will be advertised at the same time as matched prefixes are withdrawn.\\n* The allow and drop actions are terminal. When a route matches either one, no further rules are evaluated for that route. Other actions, such as set-med and summarize, are non-terminal, so processing continues. A route that reaches the end of all rules without matching a terminal action is allowed, with any modifications applied.\\n* Segment share policies are applied after attachment policies.\\n* Routing policies associated across segments and Regions are unidirectional.\\n* Routing policies are not supported for network function groups (service insertion).\\n\\n### Attachment type support\\n\\n* VPC attachments don't support BGP attribute modification.\\n* Summarization only works outbound and on BGP-capable attachments.\\n* No BGP community support on Direct Connect and TGW peering attachments.\\n* TGW route table attachments that use the same peering and are associated with the same segment share the same outbound routing policies across all similar attachments. For example, if attachment-1 has outbound routing policy 1 on segment prod and peering 1, and attachment-2 has outbound routing policy 2 on the same segment and peering, both policies apply to both attachments.\\n\\n### BGP and ASN constraints\\n\\n* ASNs specified in the routing policy (replace/remove ASN, community tags) cannot overlap with the ASN range specified in the core network configuration. This also means you cannot advertise communities into a core network that contain an ASN currently in use by the core network.\\n* Replace ASN is not supported cross-Region (CNE-to-CNE).\\n* External AWS devices cannot advertise routes with BGP communities containing internal ASNs.\\n* Route summarization does not preserve the BGP attributes of the matched prefixes. The summarized route is advertised as a new route with reset attribute values: MED of 100, local-preference of 0, an empty AS-path, and empty communities.\\n\\n### Prefix lists and visibility\\n\\n* Prefix list aliases must be unique per prefix list core network association.\\n* Prefix list modifications of entry values to the underlying core network routing state may not align with the prefix list state.\\n* The `list-core-network-routing-information` API shows the routing information before routing policies have been applied\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-routing-policies.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Running Verify Aws Claim"}

{"id": "ded9f13f-f331-4b56-af98-5ec5f5bad276", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "## How Cloud WAN picks the path for that aggregate prefix

Cloud WAN evaluates routes at each core network edge in a strict priority order:

1. **Most specific prefix wins** — this is the first and biggest factor. If the local DX gateway is only advertising the aggregate (summarized) prefix, and a *more specific* route to the same destination exists via another region, Cloud WAN will pick the more specific one over your aggregate, even if the aggregate is local.
2. If there are multiple routes to the **exact same prefix**, it then breaks the tie by target type:
   - Static routes
   - System routes (1:1 NAT)
   - VPC‑propagated routes in the **same region**
   - For dynamic (BGP) routes with **unequal AS path length or MED**, it prefers shorter AS path, then lower MED
   - Only if AS path and MED are **equal** does it fall back to source-type preference: Direct Connect gateway–propagated routes → Connect attachments in the same region → Site‑to‑Site VPN in the same region → everything else (including CNE‑to‑CNE routes from remote regions over AWS backbone)
   - If routes are still identical, it picks a single attachment **deterministically at random** — which is likely what you're seeing: the aggregate is tied across your local DX and a remote-region path, and the random tiebreak is sending it out-of-region.

So the "leaving the region" behavior is almost always one of two causes:
- **The remote region is advertising a more specific prefix** than your local DX's aggregate, so it wins on specificity before source-type is even considered, or
- **The routes are tied on AS path/MED**, landing in the random tiebreak bucket, which can non-deterministically send some segments/network function groups out over the remote-region path instead of local DX.

## How to make the local DX win

- **Make the local Direct Connect gateway advertise the more specific prefixes**, not just the aggregate — specificity beats everything else in evaluation, so this is the most reliable fix.
- If you must keep advertising only the aggregate, **shorten the AS path or lower the MED** on the local DX's BGP advertisement relative to the remote-region path, so it wins at the AS-path/MED stage before the random tiebreak is reached.
- You can also use a **Cloud WAN routing policy** to `set-med` on the DX gateway attachment's outbound advertisement to bias it lower (more preferred) than the remote-region route — note BGP attribute modification isn't supported on VPC attachments, and DX/TGW peering attachments don't support BGP communities, but MED-setting via routing policy on the DX attachment is viable.
- Confirm there's no static route or VPC-propagated same-region route interfering first, since those outrank dynamic BGP routes entirely regardless of DX preference.

Want me to check your actual core network's routing policies and the specific prefixes being advertised from each region to pinpoint which of these is happening?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
